subject: Order form commercial reconciliation: pricing cadence, tax residence, and net-term trigger mechanics
messages:
From: Andrea Rossi <andrea.rossi@helixcloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@helixcloud.com
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: clarification on invoicing cadence, net terms trigger, and tax residency

Jonas, thanks for the draft order form. A few points finance needs clarified before we can route this to procurement: 

1) Net terms trigger — we need to confirm whether net-45 (as discussed) is applied per-invoice issuance or per-commit tranche. In Helix's ERP we need a stable trigger for cashflow forecasting.

2) Invoicing cadence — you have an annual up-front option and quarterly invoicing for staged commits. Can you confirm the exact invoice dates if we pick the quarterly route? We need month-day alignment for our accounting close.

3) Tax / VAT responsibility — Helix is EU-registered and will need to confirm whether Redwood will treat us as VAT-reverse-charge or if Redwood will charge VAT. Please confirm the evidence Redwood requires (certificate or VAT ID) and whether Redwood will accept our EU VAT certificate as sufficient.

Attached: Helix_OrderForm_v2.pdf, VAT_Residence_Cert_helix.pdf

Would appreciate concise answers so we can finalize the PO.

Thanks,
Andrea Rossi
Head of Finance, HelixCloud
Attachment: Helix_OrderForm_v2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: VAT_Residence_Cert_helix.pdf (pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Andrea Rossi <andrea.rossi@helixcloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: clarification on invoicing cadence, net terms trigger, and tax residency

Andrea — thanks for the clear list. Answers inline and action items below.

1) Net terms trigger: Redwood applies net terms per-issued invoice. For staged/min-commit tranches we will issue an invoice at the start of each tranche (invoice date = tranche start). If you need terms that apply from service activation rather than invoice date we can discuss, but that would be an exception requiring Legal sign-off.

2) Invoicing cadence: For quarterly invoicing we propose the following alignment: invoices issued on the 1st business day of the quarter (Jan 1 / Apr 1 / Jul 1 / Oct 1) and due net-45 from invoice date. If your accounting needs a specific month-day (e.g., 15th), we can shift to 15th-of-quarter billing, but that would change cashflow for Redwood and needs Ops sign-off.

3) VAT / Tax evidence: Acceptable evidence = EU VAT number + a copy of the VAT certificate. Kimberly, Laura — can you confirm Redwood's standard ask here? My understanding: if Helix provides a valid EU VAT ID and certificate, Redwood will not charge VAT and will process as reverse-charge (Helix self-accounts). We will, however, require the VAT ID on the PO and the billing entity to match the certificate.

Action items:
- Kimberly to confirm acceptable evidence and update order form appendix (Attachments: Pricing_Schedule_2025.xlsx).
- Laura (Legal) to confirm whether net terms per-invoice is acceptable or if Helix's requested net-from-activation needs a contract exception.
- Ben to propose final signing route (DocuSign vs emailed countersign).

I attached an updated pricing schedule with the quarterly invoice dates filled in (Pricing_Schedule_2025.xlsx). If that aligns, can Helix confirm the billing entity and PO number so we can send to legal for the order form signature?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Jonas Weber | +1 415-555-0198
Attachment: Pricing_Schedule_2025.xlsx (xlsx)

DocuSign is preferred for speed. I'll prepare the order form for DocuSign once we confirm: billing entity, exact PO number, and whether you accept reverse-charge treatment based on the VAT certificate.
